text:
Matthew Schaefer's fight with Luke Hughes in Saturday's 5-4 overtime loss to the Devils got the most clicks, but the more telling Schaefer line was the one Stefen Rosner posted afterward: on the overtime non-call, "I thought I [got tripped], but I mean, they could have seen otherwise." He's the player the whole operation leans on now, and the pair he shares with Logan Stanley is on the right side of the chances (56 percent).

The trouble is around him. Ryan Pulock is out two to four weeks with an upper-body injury, which leaves a defense that was already giving up plenty without one of its veterans. The Islanders take 46 percent of the expected goals overall (the quality of chances) and are winless in three, outscored 14-7 on chances that back the result.

What's kept them at 7-6-3 is goaltending. Their goalies have stopped about nine more goals than the chances against them would predict, and Semyon Varlamov in particular has been better than his save rate looks, 5.0 goals saved above expected over his last five starts. That's a thin cushion to build a season on. Our simulations give the Islanders a 20 percent playoff chance, and the honest read is that the goalies are doing their part and the skaters aren't yet.
headline: The Islanders have a teenage star and a thin blue line
